title: Significance of Halal Earnings in Islam
summary: The Prophet emphasized that only pure earnings and deeds are accepted by Allah.
translation: Then pure earnings and lawful earnings are spent at a rightful place and appropriate occasion. That's why the close companion of the Holy Prophet, Abdullah bin Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), once said that when the earnings are pure, the expenditure will be pure too. Therefore, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) mentioned many sayings in this regard, including a hadith in which the Prophet stated: 'O people, Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure.' Furthermore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: "O messengers, eat from the good things and do righteous deeds. Surely, I am aware of what you do." And He said, "O you who believe, eat from the good things We have provided for you."' The Prophet stated that Allah has given the same command to believers as He did to the messengers. Addressing the messengers, He said to consume pure sustenance and do good deeds. Mentioning both together implies that consuming pure food inspires good deeds. If a person does not consume pure food, the ability to do good deeds is taken away. Then, in the Quran, it is mentioned that surely, whatever you do, I am aware of it. Similarly, Allah said regarding the believers, 'O believers, eat from the pure sustenance We provided for you.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) described a person who is coming from a long journey, disheveled and covered in dust, and in a state of distress, raises his hands towards the sky saying, 'O Lord, O Lord,' while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothes are unlawful, and his nourishment is unlawful. So how can his prayer be accepted due to all these reasons? Therefore, consuming pure and lawful sustenance leads to pure deeds that are acceptable to Allah, whereas consuming unlawful wealth ruins deeds, making them unworthy of acceptance by Allah.
